subject: Prod throughput drop — silent quota floor causing throttling
messages:
From: Emma Walsh <emma@clearlytics.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, support@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 21 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: High tail latency and 503 spikes affecting ingestions

Hi Jordan / Redwood support team,

We saw a sudden increase in end-to-end latency starting ~08:40 PDT this morning. Our ingestion pipeline (burst to 700 req/s for ~4m) hit a cascade of 5xx responses from the Redwood API and client-side retries that doubled our QPS. After throttling we observed long tail latencies (500ms -> 2.1s) and a small but consistent drop in throughput (down ~18%). Attached is a trimmed request trace (request-trace-20260421.jsonl.gz).

Is there a recent change to quota/burst windows on your side? This is impacting our consumer batch window and will affect SLAs if unresolved. We need a mitigation ETA.

Thanks,
Emma Walsh

Subject: Re: Fwd: High tail latency and 503 spikes affecting ingestions

Jordan / team — quick findings from the trace and metrics:

- We see a spike in incoming QPS from Clearlytics at 08:38; their client retries amplified to ~1.4k rps for ~3m.
- Our token-bucket-based quota meter for the tenant exercised a "safety floor" that prevents bursts above X tokens/sec when sustained token debt exceeds threshold. That floor kicked in because their burst collided with an internal pacing window update that ran at 08:35, which temporarily reduced the burst allowance.
- The safety floor is behaving as designed but is too conservative in the presence of short client bursts; requests were being accepted but immediately rate-limited (503) because the bucket checked against an adjusted window size.

Immediate mitigation suggestion: temporarily raise their burst allowance and disable the recent burst-window enforcer for the tenant while we patch the pacing rollback logic. I can push a hotfix to the quota controller to relax the debt threshold for 30 minutes.

I'll start the patch and post logs/PR.

-Marcus

Subject: Update: mitigation applied and follow-up next steps

Hi Emma / Jake — quick update from yesterday's escalation.

What we did: 
- At 10:25 PDT we applied a manual override to increase your burst ceiling for tenant CLE-4783 and disabled the new burst-window enforcer for 45 minutes.
- At 10:30 PDT Marcus rolled a hotfix to the quota controller that relaxes the debt threshold for short-lived bursts; rollout completed 10:36 PDT.
- We observed error rates fall from ~6% -> <0.5% within 8 minutes and p95 latency returned to baseline. No further 5xx spikes were seen during the observation window.

Next steps: 
1) We'll keep the monitoring rule active for 48 hours and then reinstate the corrected enforcer with a smaller window.
2) Marcus will propose a config change to the pacing update cadence to avoid overlapping updates during high QPS windows (INF-2347).
3) Laura and I will follow up on any SLA impact and credit assessment by EOD tomorrow.

I've attached the mitigation plan and the snapshot we used. Let us know if you still see anomalies. Appreciate the patience and the detailed traces — they helped us pinpoint the race between client burst and pacing update.

Regards,
Jordan Blake
